subject.title: [Bug]: Task and Memory Recall Is Often Too Weak to Trust Across Real Conversations

question: Should OpenClaw define reliable project/task memory as default core behavior now, document it as a workspace/plugin pattern, or split this umbrella into narrower memory-engine and session-recall fixes first?
rationale: Current main has partial opt-in primitives, but there is no established default project/task state contract and broader transcript recall has privacy and product-boundary tradeoffs automation should not choose.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Tracks
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical reliability report while maintainers create focused child work for task-state capture, session recall, ranking, diagnostics, and live QA proof.

options.title: Sponsor A Core Reliability Contract
options.body: Define a product contract for project/task memory capture, mutation precedence, recall defaults, privacy scope, and ship it with docs and live validation.

options.title: Document Workspace Or Plugin Pattern
options.body: If default task memory should stay outside core, convert the request into a documented reliability pack or plugin pattern rather than adding more core behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical reliability report while maintainers create focused child work for task-state capture, session recall, ranking, diagnostics, and live QA proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent and historical trail across memory-search defaults, session memory, and docs for routing the product decision.
